jobs.title: Director of Community Engagement, Alpha - $400,000/year USD
jobs.description:
Families who enroll at Alpha rarely find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—sitting across a dinner table—told them, "This made a difference for our child." You will own that word-of-mouth system for an entire region: the gatherings, the parent champions, the relationship with the mayor's office, the CEO who provides a 14-year-old with their first meaningful project.

Your typical week involves four distinct environments. You create and execute the regional event calendar, ranging from 150-person open houses to eight-person curated dinners, running several each month. You identify and train current parents eager to share their experiences with prospective families, then broker one-to-one connections. You cultivate ties with municipal leaders and corporate executives, converting them into event venues, allies for campus expansions, and tangible pathways for students. And you fulfill the Alpha Networks promise: brokered introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internship placements, alumni integration, tracked meticulously family by family.

No complete playbook exists. You develop it in real time, and the frameworks you create become templates for colleagues building identical engines in other markets. As your region expands, the challenge intensifies: doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth attributable to personal endorsements, evaluated over years rather than quarters.

No degree is mandatory, and no specific background is preferred. An MBA, a career in consulting or wealth management, and a self-directed path in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight. What matters is a demonstrated history of convening people and converting relationships into outcomes.

This position is based on-site in one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. The role includes evening and weekend events with high-expectation parents, elected officials, and entrepreneurs, plus frequent local travel. You will become the most networked individual in your city, and you will invest that capital in students. If that exchange feels purposeful rather than burdensome, apply.

What You Will Be Doing

Creating and executing the regional event calendar: public open events, curated dinners segmented by city and grade level, and family retreats, multiple times per month within budget
Arranging venues, hosts, and vendors, then serving as live host during each event
Identifying current parents to serve as ambassadors, arming them with authentic narratives, and pairing them with prospective families and campus tours
Establishing connections with municipal officials and corporate leaders, and converting those relationships into event venues, campus launch support, and opportunities for students
Pairing enrolled families into parent circles and students into mentorships, expert-led masterclasses, and professional internships, and integrating graduating families into the alumni network within 30 days
Recording every event, introduction, and referral source in the CRM (customer relationship management platform) to ensure "doors opened per family" is measurable and accurate

What You Won’t Be Doing

Purchasing growth. No paid advertising, no media budget, no impression or lead-generation metrics
Managing brand narrative or centralized campaigns; that belongs to Marketing
Handling admissions logistics, conducting tours, or managing enrollment documentation; Admissions and Family Success own that
Operating a campus on a daily basis, or managing the physical facility
Presenting raw attendance figures and headcount as if a filled room were the objective
Waiting for a finalized playbook, a template, or additional staff before launching

Director Of Community Engagement Key Responsibilities

Drive people-driven referrals as the primary source of enrollment growth in your region.

Basic Requirements

5+ years creating communities or relationship-driven programs in K-12 education, membership organizations, or similar network businesses, where growth originated from people: referrals, members, congregations, chapters, alumni, or a client portfolio, with quantifiable results
Personally planned and executed 20+ events spanning the full spectrum, from intimate curated dinners to 100+ attendee open events, with full budget responsibility
Established and sustained relationships with public officials or corporate executives that delivered specific, identifiable value
Consistent CRM practitioner; tracking relationships, attributions, and activities is already standard practice
Currently resides in, or willing to relocate to, one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich (CT), Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado (PR), Nashville, or Park City (UT)
Eligible to work in the US without requiring visa sponsorship

Nice-to-have Requirements

Led regional growth, community, or partnership initiatives for a network-structured organization: a school network, membership club, franchise, or faith or civic body
Developed and leveraged a high-trust relationship portfolio as a client-facing leader in wealth management, consulting, or business development
Advanced through admissions, advancement, community organizing, or hospitality, and consistently served as the institutional representative and host
Pre-existing connections with local government or the business ecosystem in your city
Deep understanding of how families navigate high-stakes education choices

About Alpha

Join the team building school around student growth

Alpha reimagines the school day around faster learning, stronger mentorship, and more time for students to build real-world skills.

Roles with real student impact:
Alpha hires teachers (guides), operators, admissions experts, school & curriculum leaders, and remote team members.

Education work that pays like it matters:
Alpha offers six-figure roles for people ready to help build a radically better school experience.

A culture built for builders:
Alpha is fast-moving, ambitious, and student focused. It’s for people who want to improve the system, not maintain it.

Alpha is where you can do the most meaningful work of your career.

There is so much to cover for this exciting role, and space here is limited. Hit the Apply button if you found this interesting and want to learn more. We look forward to meeting you!

Working with us

Youtube
Hugging Face

Role Overview

Nanonets is building a broader partner ecosystem to expand our enterprise reach and make
partnerships a meaningful source of pipeline, revenue, and customer value.
This is a new role designed to help turn that strategy into a working partner operation.
You will work closely with Nanonets leadership and our strategic ecosystem advisor to build
and manage the programs, processes, and operating rhythm needed to support multiple types
of partners. These will include global and regional systems integrators, consulting firms,
technology partners, ERP ecosystem partners, referral partners, and other strategic
relationships.

platform. We are looking for a partnership generalist who understands how different partner
models work and can translate strategy into partner plans, enablement, joint go-to-market
activity, qualified pipeline, and revenue.

operating model while also helping a focused group of priority partners produce measurable
business results.

What You’ll Do

Build the Partner Operating Model

• Help put Nanonets’ partner strategy, program structure, and operating model into
practice

enablement, business planning, opportunity management, and performance reviews

integrators, consulting firms, technology companies, referral partners, and strategic
solution partners

executive checkpoints, and quarterly business reviews

executive sponsorship, enablement, joint account planning, and revenue objectives

alliances, solution development, and executive leadership

opportunities, and measurable results

Drive Partner-Sourced Revenue

activity between partners and the Nanonets sales organization
• Build visibility into partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline
• Help partners position Nanonets within enterprise transformation, automation, finance,
operations, and supply-chain initiatives
• Support active opportunities and remove the commercial, organizational, or technical
obstacles that can slow partner-led deals
• Track partner contribution to pipeline, bookings, revenue, and strategic account
penetration

Enable and Scale

• Create practical enablement materials that help partner sellers, consultants, architects,
and delivery teams understand where Nanonets fits and how to take it to market
• Coordinate partner training, solution workshops, sales plays, use-case development, and
field activation
• Work with Marketing to develop partner campaigns, events, customer stories, and
market-facing content
• Help build repeatable solutions around high-value enterprise workflows such as
accounts payable, procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, order management, and customs
documentation

partner program

Support Commercial Development

managed-platform, and strategic solution relationships
• Support partnership agreements, business cases, investment decisions, and commercial
negotiations
• Understand partner economics and create structures that give both Nanonets and its
partners a clear reason to invest
• Ensure that commercial arrangements are tied to specific commitments, responsibilities,
and expected outcomes

Collaborate Cross-Functionally

• Work closely with Sales to connect partner activity to target accounts and active
opportunities
• Partner with Product and Engineering teams to communicate partner requirements and
prioritize high-value integrations and capabilities
• Coordinate with Marketing on joint positioning, campaigns, events, and market
development
• Work with Customer Success and delivery teams to support strong customer handoffs
and successful implementations
• Collaborate with Finance and Legal on commercial structures, agreements, governance,
and reporting

Requirements:

Broad Partnership Experience

• 8–12 years of experience in enterprise software partnerships, alliances, business
development, or partner-led go-to-market roles
• Experience working across more than one partner model, such as systems integrators,
consulting firms, technology alliances, ERP platforms, referral partners, or channel
relationships
• Strong understanding of how enterprise partners sell, influence customer decisions,
develop solutions, and deliver services
• Experience working with global or regional systems integrators and enterprise
consulting organizations

Proven Execution

operating processes, partner activity, and commercial results

enablement programs, and partner governance

Executive Presence and Operating Discipline

Enterprise Technology Understanding

or related software categories
Understanding of enterprise platforms such as SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Infor,

Global and Available

Additional Information

This is a hybrid role based in the Bay Area, California, with an expectation of working from our

jobs.description:
About Treeswift

In the face of rising threats, increasing pressure on affordability, and unprecedented demand for power, Treeswift empowers energy companies to modernize their field work to meet the growth and challenges ahead.

We build physical AI for the field worker: whether on foot or in a vehicle, our technology is an ironman suit for engineers, linemen, and vegetation crews: same worker, same boots on the ground, now operating at 10x productivity. Our platform is powered by cutting edge hardware, sensors (LiDAR, camera, etc…), AI and software designed to revolutionize work in the toughest environments.

Since our first pilot with a utility in June 2024, we've grown fast, now working with three of the five largest utilities in the US. To date, our technology has enabled our customers to reduce wildfire risk, regulatory and outage risk from vegetation, avoid delays and cost overruns in new construction, and accelerate recovery from severe storms.

To tackle this challenge, we are bringing together a team of mission-driven experts with deep industry experience in robotics (Penn, Caltech, CMU) and enterprise software development (Palantir, Stripe, Oracle, MongoDB). We have raised funding from leading investors including Penny Pritzker’s Inspired Capital.

We are headquartered in midtown Manhattan, with additional offices in San Francisco and Philadelphia.

Our growth is only accelerating. We’re looking for deeply curious and highly ambitious people who want to have a real world impact. Come build the future of (field) work with us.

The Position:

We're hiring a Chief of Staff to work directly alongside our CEO as a true extension of their judgment, network, and execution. This is not an administrative or project management role; your primary objective is to increase the leverage of the CEO as a strategic operator. That means building and managing executive relationships across the utility industry, ensuring the CEO is spending time with the right people at the right moments, and developing a deep enough understanding of Treeswift's business and strategy to help the CEO drive the company's most important priorities internally.

You'll own the operating cadence around the CEO's external relationships, proactively identifying who they should meet, orchestrating introductions, managing outreach, preparing them for conversations, and ensuring follow-up actually happens. You'll also step in to represent the CEO credibly in front of clients and partners and own high-priority strategic projects that cut across the company. Internally, you'll help the CEO turn company strategy into action, working across sales, operations, engineering, and leadership to surface issues, drive decisions, and make sure the highest-priority work moves forward. This person will often be the CEO's stand-in in external-facing conversations, and needs to build trust with technical, operational, and executive audiences alike.

This role requires someone who naturally operates with high agency. We want someone who notices what should happen next and makes it happen without waiting for direction.

If you're energized by building relationships, thrive in ambiguous environments, and want a front-row seat to building one of the world's leading physical AI companies, we'd love to talk.

What You'll Do:

Multiply the CEO's effectiveness

Own the CEO's external operating system, including outreach, relationship management, meeting preparation, follow-up, and long-term engagement strategy

Leads a four-person Development and Membership team and oversees approximately $2.4 million in FY27 contributed, special-event, and sponsorship revenue, in addition to the capital campaign.

ABOUT THE MUSIC HALL The Music Hall is a beloved nonprofit arts and cultural organization in downtown Portsmouth, New Hampshire. Since opening as a vaudeville theater in 1878, it has grown into a vibrant gathering place for live music, comedy, film, literary events, education programs, and community experiences. Today, The Music Hall welcomes more than 130,000 patrons each year across its Historic Theater, Music Hall Lounge, New Hampshire Film Festival, and year-round member and community programming.

ABOUT THE ROLE The Music Hall is seeking a collaborative, strategic, and relationship-driven Director of Development to lead philanthropy at one of New England’s treasured arts and cultural institutions. This senior leader will be accountable for growing contributed revenue, deepening donor and member relationships, and supporting The Music Hall’s mission to bring people together through exceptional arts, culture, and community experiences.

Working closely with the President & CEO, Board of Trustees, and colleagues across the organization, the Director of Development will lead and be accountable for major gifts, membership, sponsorship, grants, planned giving, special events, and capital support. The role includes personally managing a portfolio of principal and major-gift prospects, leading the Development and Membership team, and directing completion of The Music Hall’s current capital campaign.

The Music Hall is advancing the remaining phase of its Treasure the Legacy campaign, originally set at $15 million and expanded to $18 million to include the acquisition of Kearsarge House. Approximately $13.2 million has been raised toward the $18 million goal. The remaining phase will support community accessibility, safety, ADA compliance, and historic preservation work. The Director of Development will maintain campaign momentum while strengthening the major-gift, membership, sponsorship, grants, and planned-giving infrastructure that supports the organization beyond the campaign.

As part of The Music Hall leadership team, this role collaborates on strategic planning, organizational culture, and institution-wide priorities while advancing The Music Hall’s mission, vision, and core values. Under the direction of the President & CEO, the Director of Development also serves as the primary staff partner to the Board of Trustees Development Committee and designated campaign committees.

The successful candidate will bring a demonstrated record of growing annual contributed revenue, personally cultivating and closing major gifts, leading a capital or comprehensive campaign, increasing donor retention, strengthening membership and institutional giving, deepening corporate partnerships, and building a culture of philanthropy across an organization.
This is an opportunity for an experienced fundraising leader who loves the arts, values community, and enjoys building lasting relationships with donors, members, sponsors, trustees, and civic partners.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES Fundraising Leadership

Lead and be accountable for a comprehensive contributed-revenue program, including major gifts, membership, sponsorship, grants, planned giving, events, and capital support.
Direct the remaining phase of The Music Hall’s current capital campaign while strengthening the fundraising systems that will support the organization long term.
Partner with the President & CEO, trustees, and senior staff on donor strategy, cultivation, solicitation, closing, and stewardship.
Personally manage a portfolio of principal and major-gift prospects and lead the cultivation, solicitation, closing, and stewardship of significant gifts.
Prepare thoughtful donor briefings, proposals, recognition opportunities, and follow-up plans.
Use Music Hall programming, member experiences, the New Hampshire Film Festival, and private gatherings to build meaningful donor engagement.

Team, Board, and Community Partnership

Supervise, support, and develop the Development and Membership team; establish clear responsibilities and performance goals; manage the department budget; evaluate staff performance; and recommend staffing or structural changes to the President & CEO.
Under the direction of the President & CEO, serve as the primary staff partner to the Board Development Committee and related campaign committees, equipping trustees and volunteers for effective cultivation and solicitation.
Work collaboratively with marketing, communications, finance, programming, membership, box office, and operations colleagues.
Develop clear, compelling donor and sponsor communications for print, digital, and website use.
Build strong relationships with donors, members, sponsors, trustees, volunteers, and community partners.

Planning, Data, and Stewardship

Set measurable annual revenue, retention, portfolio, pipeline, and activity goals and create practical plans to achieve them.
Manage the Development budget and oversee fundraising reports, dashboards, forecasts, and campaign projections, reporting progress and corrective actions to the President & CEO.
Maintain strong donor data, pipeline tracking, and stewardship practices, with a clearly assigned primary relationship manager for each significant donor or prospect.
Ensure clear staff ownership and accountability for grants and institutional giving, including prospect research, funder relationships, calendars, applications, reports, compliance, and renewals.
Represent The Music Hall’s mission, values, and community-centered spirit with professionalism and care.

QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience; advanced degree welcome but not required.
At least seven years of progressively responsible nonprofit fundraising experience, including experience leading and developing fundraising professionals.
Direct leadership experience in a capital or comprehensive campaign, including campaign strategy, prospect pipeline development, forecasting, volunteer leadership, and personal solicitation.
Demonstrated success personally cultivating, soliciting, and closing major gifts, together with broad experience across individual giving, membership, sponsorship, grants, and institutional giving.
Strong relationship-building, communication, planning, budgeting, and board-engagement skills.
Experience with CRM databases and donor research tools; Salesforce and PatronManager experience preferred.
Comfort working in a lively arts and cultural environment, including some evenings and weekends.
Ability to manage confidential information, complex details, and time-sensitive work with care.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS CFRE and/or CAP credential.
Experience in a performing arts, cultural, or membership-based nonprofit organization.
Experience with planned giving, grant strategy, and digital fundraising tools.

Benefits include health and dental insurance, paid time off, parking, 401(k), employee wellness reimbursement, complimentary tickets, cell-phone support, and eligibility for the sabbatical program, subject to current plan terms.

Job Description

Executive Director, Office of Community Outreach and Engagement, Stanford Cancer Institute - Hybrid

Background

The Stanford Cancer Institute (SCI) is a national and international leader in cancer research across the cancer control continuum, with a strong commitment to serving the more than 7.8 million people in the San Francisco Bay Area through cutting-edge patient-centered cancer care, innovative research, cancer-focused community outreach and engagement, and impactful research translation. Our catchment area, where 79% of our patients reside, includes 10 geographically adjacent and highly diverse counties with respect to race/ethnicity, age, immigrant status, and population density. Community partners, COE staff, and SCI leadership defined our high priority cancers for research and control over the short term (breast, lung, pancreas, colorectal, prostate), as well as priority targets for cancer prevention including obesity and tobacco control.

Position Summary

The Executive Director (Academic Program Professional 3) will be responsible for leading the Office of Community Outreach and Engagement at the Stanford Cancer Institute. This is an exciting opportunity for an individual to direct a multi-level collaborative effort to reduce the overall cancer burden and cancer disparities in our catchment area and beyond.

This position will work closely with the Associate Director of the Office of Community Outreach and Engagement (COE), Professor Alyce S. Adams, and other leaders to align SCI research with the needs of the communities living in the 10 counties in Northern California served by SCI. Under the supervision of the AD, the position will execute the COE strategic plan to carry out community outreach and engagement activities as articulated in the Cancer Center Support Grant (CCSG) sponsored by the National Cancer Institute. Aims of SCI COE are to: 1. Understand and monitor the cancer burden, 2. Developing bidirectional relationships to advance cancer control in the community, 3. Fostering research, including enhancing representation in clinical trials, and 4. Translating research into practice and policy change that promote community health. The short and long-term impact of the proposed activities will be evaluated using theoretically and empirically supported frameworks and metrics in close collaboration with the SCI Community Advisory Board, community partners and SCI leadership.

This position will work collaboratively with the rest of the SCI leadership team to lead the COE administrative structure, develop processes and to lead key initiatives.

Families who enroll at Alpha rarely find us through advertising. They come because someone they trust—sitting across a dinner table—told them, "This made a difference for our child." You will own that word-of-mouth system for an entire region: the gatherings, the parent champions, the relationship with the mayor's office, the CEO who provides a 14-year-old with their first meaningful project.

Your typical week involves four distinct environments. You create and execute the regional event calendar, ranging from 150-person open houses to eight-person curated dinners, running several each month. You identify and train current parents eager to share their experiences with prospective families, then broker one-to-one connections. You cultivate ties with municipal leaders and corporate executives, converting them into event venues, allies for campus expansions, and tangible pathways for students. And you fulfill the Alpha Networks promise: brokered introductions, expert-led masterclasses, internship placements, alumni integration, tracked meticulously family by family.

No complete playbook exists. You develop it in real time, and the frameworks you create become templates for colleagues building identical engines in other markets. As your region expands, the challenge intensifies: doors opened per family must increase even as total enrollment grows. Success is measured by the proportion of growth attributable to personal endorsements, evaluated over years rather than quarters.

No degree is mandatory, and no specific background is preferred. An MBA, a career in consulting or wealth management, and a self-directed path in community building, hospitality, or institutional advancement all carry equal weight. What matters is a demonstrated history of convening people and converting relationships into outcomes.

This position is based on-site in one of these regions: San Francisco, Los Angeles, San Diego, Denver, Greenwich, Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Oklahoma City, Tulsa, Dorado, Nashville, or Park City. This role requires someone who naturally operates with high agency. We want someone who notices what should happen next and makes it happen without waiting for direction.

ABOUT THE MUSIC HALL The Music Hall is a beloved nonprofit arts and cultural organization in downtown Portsmouth, New Hampshire. Since opening as a vaudeville theater in 1878, it has grown into a vibrant gathering place for live music, comedy, film, literary events, education programs, and community experiences. Today, The Music Hall welcomes more than 130,000 patrons each year across its Historic Theater, Music Hall Lounge, New Hampshire Film Festival, and year-round member and community programming.

ABOUT THE ROLE The Music Hall is seeking a collaborative, strategic, and relationship-driven Director of Development to lead philanthropy at one of New England’s treasured arts and cultural institutions. This senior leader will be accountable for growing contributed revenue, deepening donor and member relationships, and supporting The Music Hall’s mission to bring people together through exceptional arts, culture, and community experiences.

Working closely with the President & CEO, Board of Trustees, and colleagues across the organization, the Director of Development will lead and be accountable for major gifts, membership, sponsorship, grants, planned giving, special events, and capital support. The role includes personally managing a portfolio of principal and major-gift prospects, leading the Development and Membership team, and directing completion of The Music Hall’s current capital campaign.

The Music Hall is advancing the remaining phase of its Treasure the Legacy campaign, originally set at $15 million and expanded to $18 million to include the acquisition of Kearsarge House. Approximately $13.2 million has been raised toward the $18 million goal. The remaining phase will support community accessibility, safety, ADA compliance, and historic preservation work. The Director of Development will maintain campaign momentum while strengthening the major-gift, membership, sponsorship, grants, and planned-giving infrastructure that supports the organization beyond the campaign.

As part of The Music Hall leadership team, this role collaborates on strategic planning, organizational culture, and institution-wide priorities while advancing The Music Hall’s mission, vision, and core values. Under the direction of the President & CEO, the Director of Development also serves as the primary staff partner to the Board of Trustees Development Committee and designated campaign committees.

The successful candidate will bring a demonstrated record of growing annual contributed revenue, personally cultivating and closing major gifts, leading a capital or comprehensive campaign, increasing donor retention, strengthening membership and institutional giving, deepening corporate partnerships, and building a culture of philanthropy across an organization.

new_jobs.title: Regional Director of Community Engagement
new_jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Regional Director of Community Engagement serves as a key regional liaison, building and sustaining strong internal partnerships across the agency from mid level leadership through senior leadership, and strategic external partnerships with community organizations, parishes, funders, and service providers to support coordinated, sustainable service delivery. All responsibilities will be performed in concert with the mission, vision and values of Catholic Charities.

Responsibilities

Directs external partnerships to support sustainability, growth, and the development of regional and agency wide service delivery

Cultivates and maintains strategic relationships with community partners, parishes, funders, and collaborating agencies to strengthen coordinated service delivery and long term viability.
Participates in the creation of the Agency’s strategic plan development, ensures partnership activities are aligned with the Agency Strategic Plan, mission, program requirements, and regional priorities; communicates partnership impacts and risks to senior leadership as needed.
Coordinates with Program Directors, Compliance, and Finance/Administration on partnership agreements (e.g., MOUs, referral pathways, facility use, and collaborative projects) to support consistent and sustainable implementation
Identifies and advances partnership opportunities that increase access, reduce duplication, and support sustainable growth of services across the region and, where applicable, agency wide.
Represents Catholic Charities professionally in designated local, regional, and national professional organizations and meetings.
Maintains a positive profile in the community with providers of other community resources.
Maintains a balance of representing all agency programs including Early Learning, Behavioral Health, Housing Services, Youth and Young Adult, Parenting, and Senior Services.
Coordinates local outreach efforts which include tabling events, resources fairs, community presentations and all external facing efforts.

Establishes and leads internal culture building efforts, supporting the local office in fostering a strong, collaborative, and mission aligned culture.

Establishes and maintains effective communication with all location agency staff, including feedback that supports program operations.
Facilitates local leadership meetings to support clear communication and cross program collaboration.
Works with local program managers to align all services with the mission and vision of Catholic Charities
Prioritizes building a strong local office culture grounded in diversity, equity, and inclusion principles, fostering belonging, respect, and shared accountability.
Coordinates with other Regional Directors of Community Engagement to promote equity, shared practices and continuity across Catholic Charities’ various locations.

Provides responsive, on the ground support to address immediate site needs in partnership with local and remote leadership.

Serves as a regional point of contact for staff, community issues, and cross program coordination.
Maintains a general understanding of regional and program budgets sufficient to communicate priorities and constraints, and to explain budget context to community stakeholders as appropriate.

Continually assesses gaps in services and community needs to identify and develop new programs and partnerships to serve underserved populations within the mission of Catholic Charities.

Supports program growth by collaborating with Program Directors and senior leadership to define the process for launching or expanding services, including regional implementation expectations, timelines, resourcing, and community readiness
Coordinates and collaborates on community needs assessments in connection with community partners in service area to assess gaps in services.

Qualifications

Job Requirements:

Physical Requirements

This position normally requires the physical demands of standing, walking, bending, lifting or performing other work requiring low physical exertion, talking and hearing on a regular basis to perform the job requirements. These physical demands are required up to 80% of the time. Position also requires the ability to drive with adequate vision.

Non Physical Requirements

Education

Bachelor's degree in communications, Social Services or closely related field required; master’s degree preferred

Experience

5 years of progressive leadership experience required

Special Skills

Ability to articulate the mission of Catholic Charities
Ability to collaborate and provide support to multi disciplinary teams
Possess and utilize effective verbal and written communication skills
Successful implementation of team leadership and staff support
Ability to be self-motivated, work independently and successfully lead and motivate teams
Ability to represent the agency in a professional manner within the community
Knowledgeable about social services best practices preferred

Licensure, Registration, Certifications

Valid Washington State driver’s license and required minimum liability insurance for WA State
Licensed or credentialed when required

Employment Is Conditional Upon

Being cleared by criminal background check and fingerprinting when required

Work Schedule:
Monday-Friday, 8:00am - 5:00pm; occasional nights & weekends when required

Wage Range:
$125,000-$145,000 per year; depending on education & experience

Benefits

13 paid holidays, 12 days of vacation, 12 days of sick leave per year
Health insurance including medical & prescription coverage, with optional dental and vision insurance plans. Majority of premiums paid by Catholic Charities
Retirement 403(b) Plan: employee contributions commence upon employment; Catholic Charities contributes 2% of monthly income and matches up to 4% of employee contributions following 6 months of employment
Basic Life Insurance paid 100% by Catholic Charities
Flexible Spending Account eligibility following 6 months of employment
Education Assistance Program reimbursing up to $5,250 per year for approved continuing education after 6 months of employment
Additional voluntary insurances including supplemental life, accidental death & dismemberment (AD&D), critical illness, long term disability, accident, and ID theft
Employee Assistance Program includes 3 counseling sessions per year, legal consultations, financial coaching, and other wellbeing tools
Annual longevity awards begin at 5 years of employment
